newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hot-tempered Japan PM fumes at nuclear miscues.
newsitem.headline: Hot-tempered Japan PM fumes at nuclear miscues.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, known in Tokyo as a blunt talker with a hot temper, has hit the boiling point twice in one week on revelations a state-run nuclear power firm has covered up atomic accidents.

"I'm disgusted," Hashimoto told reporters after learning the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) waited 30 hours before reporting a radiation leak which occurred on Monday in western Japan.
"I saw the date of the accident and the date the PNC reported. It's completely hopeless!" he said.

The remarks, made to reporters who cover the prime minister from dawn until midnight, came a week after a furious Hashimoto ordered an investigation of the PNC after it admitted falsifying a report on the worst nuclear accident to hit Japan, which occurred in March in a fire at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant.
"I am so angry I cannot utter a single word," Hashimoto, who is normally talkative and known to like sharing his insights with the cabinet press corps, said last week.
Analysts say the accidents and embarrassing bureaucratic coverups have weighed heavily on Hashimoto.
He began 1997 vowing to "go down in flames" if he failed to carry out comprehensive reforms to cut red tape and make Japan's ponderous government more responsive to its citizens.
The 59-year-old Hashimoto's reputation for tough talk was burnished when he served as trade minister and squared off against the United States in a bitter 1995 bilateral spat over cars and car parts.
